newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian shares pick up more steam, stay active.
newsitem.headline: Estonian shares pick up more steam, stay active.

text.p: The Estonian share market was at full throttle on Friday, with the index advancing by more than one percent on active trade, dealers said.
"There has been no news really, there is just more interest to Estonian stocks," said Hansapank chief equities dealer Tonu Pekk. He said there was also foreign interest in the market.
Turnover on the main list came to 15.2 million kroons and the Tallinn stock exchange index rose 1.64 percent to 100.57.
Pekk said the market would probably rise further, noting that stocks were only on six to seven times earnings.
"I do not see any threat of over-valuation yet," he added.
Savings Bank led the turnover list on volume of 6.91 million kroons, advancing to 36.25 kroons from 35 kroons.
Hansapank was second most active on 5.2 million kroons and rose well past the 100 kroon mark to end at 103 kroons after yesterday's close of 99.55 kroons.
Forexbank was also actively traded on 1.7 million kroons and it climbed to 78.30 kroons from 77.85 kroons.
Pennu computer, on its second day on the exchange, traded just over 371,000 kroons of stock and ended at 67.30 kroons after 69.60 kroons.
On the over-the-counter free market, the Rakvere meat plant traded 1.33 million kroons in a rise to 4.25 kroons from 4.05 kroons. Overall trade on the market was 5.7 million kroons.

Kalevi confectionary plant shares rose to 370 kroons from 364.5 on trade of 1.31 million kroons after a period of relative inactivity but the Norma plastics plant dipped to 23.35 kroons from 23.40 kroons on trade of 1.1 million kroons.
